key_claims: Two distinct types of brain tissue work together to support cognition in older adults.
The health of the brain's short-range wiring may help soften the cognitive effects of gray matter loss.
limitations: The source does not provide details on the study design, sample size, or statistical methods.
The source does not specify the exact nature of the cognitive effects or the degree of softening.
The source does not indicate whether the findings are causal or merely correlational.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that gray matter loss causes cognitive decline.
The study identifies a specific mechanism by which short-range wiring protects cognition.
The study provides quantitative measures of the protective effect.
The study applies to all older adults or to specific populations.
